record.context_brief: stable embedded cmc surfaces with circular boundary
record.original_question: Is every compact stable embedded constant-mean-curvature surface in R^3 with circular boundary necessarily either a planar disk or a spherical cap?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.11 (4*). Is a compact stable embedded cmc surface of R3 spanning a circle a planar disk or a spherical cap?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be a compact, smoothly embedded surface with boundary $\partial\Sigma$, and assume that $\Sigma$ has constant mean curvature $H$ (a CMC surface). Recall that $\Sigma$ is called stable if the second variation of the area functional is nonnegative for all smooth normal variations of $\Sigma$ that preserve the enclosed volume (equivalently, that have mean zero on $\Sigma$) and that fix the boundary.

Suppose further that $\partial\Sigma$ is a round circle in some plane of $\mathbb{R}^3$.

Question: Must $\Sigma$ be either a flat planar disk bounded by that circle (the case $H = 0$) or a spherical cap bounded by that circle (the case $H \neq 0$)?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is generally known as (a stable case of) the spherical cap conjecture. Partial results are known: Alías–López–Palmer proved it for stable immersed disks bounded by a circle, and Alexandrov reflection settles the case in which the embedded surface lies entirely in one closed half-space determined by the boundary plane. The general embedded stable case (allowing higher genus and surfaces crossing the boundary plane) remains open according to recent literature.

status_evidence.title: Constant mean curvature surfaces with circular boundary in R^3
status_evidence.snippet: The Spherical Cap Conjecture: ... if the surface is embedded, then it is a spherical cap. Partial results include Alexandrov reflection in the half-space case.
status_evidence.claim: States the spherical cap conjecture and lists partial results, indicating the general case is unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Surfaces with constant mean curvature in Euclidean space (survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Alías, López and Palmer proved that umbilical examples are the only stable CMC immersed disks bounded by a circle in R^3.
status_evidence.claim: Stable disk subcase is solved; embedded higher-genus case remains open.

status_evidence.title: An extension of Liebmann's Theorem to hypersurfaces with boundary
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work continues to study CMC hypersurfaces with circular/spherical boundary, referencing the spherical cap conjecture as still open in general.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2024) literature treats the spherical cap question as still open.
